topics.name: Past perfect and simple past in a story

options: The scorpion had crawled under a sack of rice.
The scorpion had crawl under a sack of rice.
The scorpion had crawling under a sack of rice.
questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle: had crawled.

options: May God blesses you with good health!
May God bless you with good health!
May God blessed you with good health!
questions.rule: In a wish starting with May, use the base verb: May God bless you!

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The participle phrase groaning with pain tells us what she was doing as she lay there.

questions.rule: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: the scorpion had already run away.

questions.before: The peasants said that the poison
questions.rule: After said, the tense moves back: is moving becomes was moving. 'Poison' is singular.
A wish or prayer for someone begins with May + subject + base verb.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a participle phrase.
questions.rule: Throwing giant shadows describes the lanterns, so it comes just before them.

chat: What did the doctor tell your grandmother?
options: He told her that she need rest.
He said her that she needed rest.
He told her that she needed rest.
questions.rule: Use told + person (said has no object) and move the tense back: needs becomes needed.

options: Mother said that she were fine.
Mother said that I was fine.
Mother said that she was fine.
questions.rule: I becomes she and am becomes was after the past reporting verb said.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Past perfect needs the past participle: had hidden. The story is in the past, so he came.

options: Father asked where the scorpion had gone.
Father asked where had the scorpion gone.
Father asked that where the scorpion had gone.
questions.rule: A reported question uses statement order (subject + verb) and no that: where the scorpion had gone.

options: Tiring after the long night, Mother fell asleep.
Tired after the long night, Mother fell asleep.
Tire after the long night, Mother fell asleep.
questions.rule: Mother felt the tiredness, so use the -ed participle: Tired after the long night.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After May in a wish, the verb stays in its base form: May the poison leave.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Told needs a person after it (told us). Without a person, use said that ...

questions.after: the scorpion indoors before it stung her.
questions.rule: The rain came first, so use the past perfect: had driven (had + past participle).

questions.before: The peasants sat around the mat,
questions.rule: An -ing participle shows an action happening at the same time: sat ..., chanting.
Reported question: asked + why + subject + verb, with no question mark.

options: May you do very well in all your papers!
May you doing very well in all your papers!
May you does very well in all your papers!
questions.rule: A good wish: May you + base verb: May you do well!

chat: Did you see the eclipse last night?
options: No, it has already ended when I reached the terrace.
No, it had already end when I reached the terrace.
No, it had already ended when I reached the terrace.
questions.rule: The eclipse ended before you reached, so use had ended (past perfect).

questions.source: It was a very dark and stormy night.
options: How a dark and stormy night it was!
What a dark and stormy night was it!
What a dark and stormy night it was!
questions.rule: Use What a + adjective + noun + subject + verb: What a dark night it was!

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: After the holy man has finished his rites, the pain slowly decreased.
After the holy man had finish his rites, the pain slowly decreased.
After the holy man had finished his rites, the pain slowly decreased.
questions.rule: The rites ended first, so use had finished; the later action is in the simple past.

options: Father told the boys that bring a lantern.
Father told the boys bring a lantern.
Father told the boys to bring a lantern.
questions.rule: A reported command uses told + person + to + verb: told the boys to bring.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Two verbs need 'and' between them; here a participle phrase is used instead: throwing long shadows.

questions.before: My little brother asked me whether the scorpion
questions.rule: After asked, has gone moves back to had gone; the past participle is gone.

questions.after: a wonderful thing a mother's love is!
questions.rule: Use What a + adjective + noun in an exclamation; How goes with an adjective alone.
The earlier action takes had fallen; the later one takes the simple past rose.

chat: What did Ravi say about the trip?
options: He said me that he could not come.
He said that he could not come.
He said that he cannot came.
questions.rule: Said takes no person after it, and can moves back to could + base verb.

chat: Why is your little sister so quiet today?
options: She is frightened after seeing a scorpion last night.
She is frightening after seeing a scorpion last night.
She is fright after seeing a scorpion last night.
questions.rule: Use -ed for how a person feels (frightened); -ing describes what causes the feeling.

questions.source: The scorpion stung Mother. Then it escaped into the rain.
options: After the scorpion had stung Mother, it escaped into the rain.
After the scorpion has stung Mother, it escaped into the rain.
After the scorpion had stinged Mother, it escaped into the rain.
questions.rule: The first action takes the past perfect: had stung (sting - stung - stung).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: After past reporting verbs, tenses move back: is - was, has gone - had gone, want - wanted.

options: Each of the villagers was holding a burning lantern.
Each of the villagers were holding a burning lantern.
Each of the villagers was hold a burning lantern.
questions.rule: Each of takes a singular verb (was), and the continuous tense needs -ing: was holding.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The verb purify goes with of: purify something of evil.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Last summer is past: he visited. The earlier state (had never seen) is in the past perfect.

questions.before: The nurse asked us how long the pain
questions.rule: A reported question has statement order with the tense moved back: how long the pain had lasted.
May + subject + base verb (be) makes a wish; it ends with an exclamation mark.

chat: You had already eaten when we called, hadn't you?
options: Yes, I hadn't. I was very hungry after the match.
Yes, I had. I were very hungry after the match.
Yes, I had. I was very hungry after the match.
questions.rule: A short answer repeats the helper verb: Yes, I had. With I, use was.

chat: Why are your clothes so wet?
options: Having walk home in the rain, I got completely wet.
Have walked home in the rain, I got completely wet.
Having walked home in the rain, I got completely wet.
questions.rule: A perfect participle is Having + past participle: Having walked home ...

questions.source: The doctor said to Father, "Take her to the hospital now."
options: The doctor told Father that take her to the hospital at once.
The doctor told Father to take her to the hospital at once.
The doctor told Father to took her to the hospital at once.
questions.rule: Command: told + person + to + base verb; now becomes at once.
How brave ... was! becomes was very brave; keep the tense and the adjective.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: 'By the time ... reached' needs had stopped. Plural neighbours takes were.

questions.prompt: Pick the correct indirect speech of: "What a terrible night!" she said.
options: She exclaimed that it was a terrible night.
She exclaimed that what a terrible night it was.
She exclaimed that it is a terrible night.
questions.rule: Reported exclamation: exclaimed that + a statement; drop 'What a' and move the tense back: it was.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: 'Having tried ...' is the earlier action; the main verb needs the simple past: Father poured.

questions.after: by the endless rain, the scorpion crawled beneath a sack of rice.
questions.rule: The scorpion was driven (passive idea) by the rain, so use the past participle Driven.
Yes/no questions are reported with whether + subject + verb (tense moved back).

chat: Grandma is going to Kashi tomorrow.
What should we say to her?
options: Let's say, 'May your journey is a peaceful one!'
Let's say, 'May your journey be a peaceful one!'
Let's say, 'May your journey being a peaceful one!'
questions.rule: In a May wish, the verb 'be' stays in its base form: May your journey be ...

questions.source: As soon as the scorpion stung Mother, it ran out into the rain.
options: No sooner did the scorpion stung Mother than it ran out into the rain.
No sooner had the scorpion stung Mother when it ran out into the rain.
No sooner had the scorpion stung Mother than it ran out into the rain.
questions.rule: Pattern: No sooner had + subject + past participle ... than + simple past.

questions.source: Mother said, "I thank God that the scorpion stung me and not my children."
options: Mother said that she thanked God that the scorpion had stung her and not her children.
Mother said that she thanked God that the scorpion had stung me and not my children.
Mother said that she thanks God that the scorpion has stung her and not her children.
questions.rule: Change I, me, my to she, her, her and move tenses back: thank - thanked, stung - had stung.

options: I pray that your suffering may ends soon.
I pray that may your suffering end soon.
I pray that your suffering may end soon.
questions.rule: A May-wish becomes I pray that + subject + may + base verb.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: I felt frightened (-ed for feelings); the story is past: tried; a participle phrase: chanted, hoping ...

questions.rule: After told, will moves back to would. The story is past, so none of them had seen it.
